key_insight: Routine clinical variables could only modestly predict albuminuria in moderate CKD, and machine-learning models did not outperform logistic regression.
clinical_relevance: These findings support continuing universal UACR testing rather than trying to replace it with prediction based on standard clinical data.
method: NHANES 2015–2018 adults with eGFR 30–59 mL/min/1.73m² were analyzed
Three models were compared: logistic regression, random forest, and gradient boosting
Performance used repeated cross-validation, calibration checks, subgroup analysis, and rule-out testing thresholds
evidence_signal: In 687 participants, all models showed similar modest discrimination (AUC about 0.72 overall), with weaker performance in people without diabetes.
watch_item: This was a survey-based observational analysis in a moderate CKD population, so the results may not generalize to other settings or replace direct urine albumin measurement in practice.
paper_title: Can Routine Clinical Variables Substitute for Urine Albumin Testing in Moderate Chronic Kidney Disease? A Machine Learning Analysis of NHANES 2015 to 2018
